assumptions: The ACTUAL_DMA_SYSTEM root top (Vnonblock_actual_dma_system_top) exposes input shared_source_cutover_i and outputs dbg_shared_cutover (1 bit), dbg_shared_cutover_vcut_bytes (J*8), dbg_shared_cutover_oldend_bytes (E*8). If the plain (non-system) top also gains these ports, the two guarded drive sites and the guarded report/verify blocks must be extended; today every §50/§54 shared-source flag is system-only, so all new code is placed inside #ifdef ACTUAL_DMA_SYSTEM.
Verilated headers must be regenerated before building, otherwise the new port references fail at compile time (no silent behaviour change is possible).

The design names no separate FA output; initial_A_cut is taken from the existing dbg_shared_cut_bytes (documented as the bytes of A's logical stream the RTL already returned), so FA beats = dbg_shared_cut_bytes/8. If the RTL instead reports FA through another port, replacement 5's strict block must read that port instead.
J and E are byte quantities (J*8 / E*8 as stated in the design), so beats = value/8; the byte-alignment CHECKs guard that truncation can never silently pass.
0<=FA holds trivially for the unsigned FA; the explicit ordering checks are FA<=J<=E<=want. The parent's requested chain is implemented exactly in that direction.

The legacy formula (bypass==3 -> 2*want; detached -> 2*want-cut; else want) is retained verbatim for the !dbg_shared_cutover case, and every other assertion in the file (content/untouched/actual logical R bytes/physical W beats/issue-done placement/pause/§54) is left byte-identical; src_expect only loses its const so the actual-cutover branch can substitute the strict value.

src_expect is declared at block scope inside the shared_source branch and the new strict branch assigns it before the single CHECK, so both the strict and the legacy CHECK operate on the same variable.

+cutover-require=1 without +source-cutover=1 is rejected at CLI level; run-time 'require => actual' is asserted in nat_verify_and_report after the real RTL outputs are final, and any failure throws before any PASS/JSON success record is printed.

This is driver-side plumbing only: no RTL, no memory model, no page tables, no existing acceptance threshold was edited; no observation is synthesised and the JSON prints only RTL outputs plus the harness's own asserted expectation.
checks: Regression (defaults): build and run the pre-existing shared run with no new flags, e.g. +natural=1 +shared-source=1 +natural-bytes=2048 +natural-trace=<f>; SOURCE-SPONSOR-HANDOVER-JSON must report opt_in=0, require_actual=0, actual=0, and derived_expected_source_r_beats must equal actual_source_r_beats and match the legacy value (want when not detached, 2*want-cut_bytes/8 when detached, 2*want under +physical-bypass=3). Byte-for-byte output of all other lines must be unchanged.

Regression (non-shared): +natural=1 +natural-bytes=32768 with the new flags absent must print the same SOURCE-SPONSOR-HANDOVER-JSON with shared_source=0, actual=0 and derived_expected_source_r_beats == want_beats; the legacy V/A source read CHECKs must still pass.

Opt-in actual path: +natural=1 +shared-source=1 +natural-bytes=2048 +shared-write-keep-q=1 +source-cutover=1 (plus trace) must compile and, when the RTL really enters the handover, the JSON must show opt_in=1, actual=1, and actual_source_r_beats == oldend_beats + (want_beats - initial_a_cut_beats) with 0<=FA<=J<=E<=want; the run must still pass every pre-existing content/untouched/logicalR/W/issue-done assertion.

Opt-in fallback path: same command without +cutover-require must pass when the RTL reports actual=0, using the legacy formula, and the JSON must show actual=0 with the legacy expected value (the documented safe fallback must not be turned into a false failure, and must not be reported as an actual cutover).

Require gate: +cutover-require=1 without +source-cutover=1 must exit 2 with '+cutover-require=1 requires +source-cutover=1'; +source-cutover=1 +cutover-require=1 on a run where dbg_shared_cutover stays 0 must fail the terminal 'actual cutover' CHECK and must not print a PASS line.
Enable gates: +source-cutover=1 must be rejected (exit 2) when combined with any of: missing +shared-source=1, missing +natural=1, +natural-bytes!=2048, +shared-write-keep-q!=1, +pause-mode>0.

Order independence: passing the flags in any permutation (e.g. +cutover-require=1 ... +source-cutover=1 vs the reverse) must yield identical accept/reject behaviour and identical JSON, because validation runs only after the whole argv loop.

Drive coverage: confirm shared_source_cutover_i is driven at both existing runtime-assign sites (Tb constructor and every tick(), including the reset ticks and the pause-block eval() calls), i.e. the input is never left x/z on the system top.

Alignment guard: the strict branch must reject non-byte-aligned dbg_shared_cutover_vcut_bytes / dbg_shared_cutover_oldend_bytes / dbg_shared_cut_bytes (exercise only by a deliberate fault injection or an RTL unit test; the real RTL is expected to be aligned).
